what: Per-engine peak WASM memory for one large raw Chronicle CSV, processed by the production build in a real browser. Recorded by web/scripts/measure_browser_peak_memory.mjs; no threshold is enforced anywhere.

producedBy.build: web/dist from `npm run build`, served by `vite preview` on 127.0.0.1:4287
producedBy.host: Apple Silicon macOS 25.2, 32 logical cores. Other agent lanes were building and running tests during these passes, so elapsedMs is wall-clock under contention and is NOT a performance claim. wasmMemoryBytes does not depend on load.

mechanics.wasmMemoryBytes: ProcessedFileResult.workerWasmMemoryBytes, recorded by the processing worker from rustWasmMemoryBytes() (WebAssembly.Memory.buffer.byteLength) when the file finished, then read back out of the app's own chronicle-last-run IndexedDB record. WASM linear memory never shrinks, so this IS the run's high-water mark, and it is exactly as accurate on WebKit and Firefox as on Chromium. Reading it from the shipped record means this measures the production path, not a private instrumentation build.
mechanics.jsHeapBytes: performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize. Chromium-only, main thread only, and it says nothing about the worker's WASM heap. Firefox and WebKit expose no equivalent to page script at all, so it is null there - that absence is part of the evidence, not a gap in the harness.
mechanics.processRss: Not recorded. Playwright's browsers are multi-process and the pipeline runs inside a worker process this harness has no reliable cross-engine way to attribute. Sampled RSS of the browsers' content processes was observed in the 0.5-3.8 GB range during these passes but is not reported as a number, because it cannot be attributed to the pipeline.
mechanics.profile: Every engine runs against an on-disk profile via launchPersistentContext. WebKit refuses OPFS in an ephemeral automation context, so an ephemeral run would measure a different (persistence-free) code path on that engine only.
mechanics.thresholds: None. This file records evidence and enforces nothing.

findings: At 34,569,498 bytes / 181,798 rows all three engines complete, and the WASM high-water mark is byte-identical across them: 1,025,900,544 B (978 MiB, 15,655 x 64 KiB pages). Peak WASM memory for this workload is a property of the Rust pipeline, not of the browser.
Row counts agree across engines as well (181,798 in / 175,131 out), which is the same cross-engine output agreement the durability suites assert.

At 115,254,808 bytes / 605,915 rows all three engines refuse the file with the SAME product error: 'reconstruction base is too large: 260554624 bytes exceeds 201326592'. 201,326,592 is MAX_RECONSTRUCTION_BASE_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES (192 MiB) in rust/chronicle_chrono_kernel_wasm/src/pipeline_v2_incremental.rs:1842, checked in encode_reconstruction_base at :2852 - the kernel's own cap on the postcard-encoded reconstruction resume value, not a browser memory limit. It is a clean fail-closed refusal with a visible message: no partial output, no silent success. The large-file ceiling is therefore set by that cap, identically on every engine, and no engine was observed to run out of memory before reaching it.

Chromium's jsHeapBytes (16.1 MB) is roughly two orders of magnitude below the worker's WASM high-water mark, which is why a main-thread heap number is not a proxy for this pipeline's memory on any engine.
